heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S handles Sunlu ASA out of the box with its fully enclosed chamber, achieving reliable print speeds up to 202 mm/s bounded by a 17 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. The stock stainless steel nozzle and 100°C heated bed are fully sufficient for non-abrasive ASA without requiring hardware upgrades.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as an interface/release agent
slicerTweaks: Set filament Max Volumetric Speed to 17 mm³/s to automatically constrain line speeds to a safe 202 mm/s ceiling.
Disable the Auxiliary Part Cooling fan completely (0%) to eliminate directional drafts that cause warping and splitting.
Preheat the bed at 98°C for 15 minutes before printing with door closed to soak the chamber to roughly 40-50°C.
Add a 5mm outer brim with a 0.1mm brim-object gap to anchor sharp corners against thermal contraction forces.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Thermal contraction caused by low chamber temperature or lack of an adhesion interface layer on PEI.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Preheat the chamber by idling the bed at 98°C for 15 minutes, apply PVA/liquid glue stick to the textured PEI sheet, and avoid opening the glass door.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Inter-layer delamination or cracking along Z-axis
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or low extrusion temperature hindering inter-layer polymer diffusion.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase nozzle temperature to 260°C, verify the auxiliary fan is off (0%), and restrict the main part cooling fan between 10% and 20% maximum.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Fine stringing and rough surface finish
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption in hygroscopic ASA filament leading to micro-steam eruptions at the nozzle tip.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dehydrate the spool in a filament dryer at 70°C for 6 to 8 hours and verify retraction distance is tuned to 0.8mm at 30mm/s.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade the Bambu Lab P1S to a hardened steel nozzle to print Sunlu ASA?
faq.answer: No, standard Sunlu ASA contains no abrasive fillers like carbon fiber or glass, making it fully compatible with the stock stainless steel nozzle.

faq.question: Should the P1S door and top glass remain open or closed during ASA printing?
faq.answer: Keep the door and top lid fully closed to trap bed heat and create an insulated chamber environment that prevents shrinkage-induced warping.

faq.question: Can Sunlu ASA be fed directly through the Bambu Lab AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, Sunlu ASA feeds smoothly through the AMS, provided plastic spools are used or cardboard spool edges are fitted with printable adapter rings.

faq.question: How should chamber ventilation be managed during printing?
faq.answer: Keep the internal carbon exhaust fan at minimal or low speed during the print to retain heat, but ventilate the room thoroughly afterwards to dissipate styrene emissions.
